_text: [fast-paced, energetic storyteller] In this world, every promise you make grows a *flower* out of your skin. [playful] Keep it, and it *blooms*. [amused] Break it, and it rots and *stinks*. [playful] You see, Linda next door ran the marathon she promised: a sunflower on her *knee*. [amused] Dad's sink promise? SIX years old. Dead tulip, on his ear. [mischievous] And the guy who said "I'll call you"? You can smell him from across the *mall*. [playful] And you? Fourteen rotten flowers, and a fly that's followed you since ninth *grade*. [deadpan] Most of them are from "I'll be there in five *minutes*." [playful] So nobody in town believes a word you *say*. [amazed] Then there's Derek: running for mayor, a THOUSAND perfect flowers, like a walking wedding cake. [playful] Every morning, he promises the town something new: free pizza, a water park, no more *Mondays*. [excited, building] And they bloom the *second* he says them. [urgent] Then one Monday, he promises to bulldoze the park, and Grandma's *beehives*. [playful] You've spent every summer on her porch, watching where those bees *go*. [determined] So, for the first time in YEARS, you promise to save them, and a bud pops out of your hand.
